summary: Console analytics: sudden loss of per-route usage metrics and tracing events after retention policy update
description:
Issue summary: FinSaaS reports that per-route usage dashboards and tracing hooks in the Console stopped showing recent events and p95/p99 charts between ~03:00-07:00 UTC. Several alert rules (per-route latency and error-rate) did not fire during an observed latency spike.

Impact: Customer-facing dashboards blank for recent window; alerts suppressed leading to delayed mitigation for increased latency. Affects FinSaaS production (enterprise tenant on dedicated capacity).

Environment: prod-us-east (customer dedicated cluster), Console v2.4.1, metrics ingestion pipeline backed by metrics-store (ClickHouse), traces via otel-collector -> trace-store (Bigtable), retention worker service: retention-sweeper v1.7.0.

Steps to reproduce:
1) Login to Console as FinSaaS admin -> open Usage > Per-route metrics for the last 6 hours.
2) Select any high-traffic route (e.g., /api/generate).
3) Observe empty time-series for the 03:00-07:00 UTC window and missing tracing events in the Traces view for the same period.
4) Check Alerting history for "fin-rt-p95-route" rule -> no notifications between 03:00-07:30 UTC despite elevated latency in raw serving logs.

Observed behavior: Metrics and traces appear to be missing (not delayed). Querying metrics-store directly returns "no rows" for ingestion time range. Retention-sweeper logs show aggressive GC for high-volume tenants executed at 02:58 UTC.

Expected behavior: Console shows continuous per-route metrics and traces; alerting evaluates using raw metrics even if some data is late. Retention job should honor per-customer retention override.

Relevant logs / links:
- Customer ticket chat: https://slack.redwood-inference.com/archives/CUS/finss-support-thread
- Metrics-store query example: https://grafana.redwood-inference.com/d/metrics-query/SUP-4821-query (internal)
- Retention worker logs (snippet): s3://redwood-logs/retention/retention-sweeper-2026-03-13.log -> shows GC for tenant_id=finss-183 with retention_days=7 applied.
comments: 2026-03-13 08:10 - Customer: We noticed our per-route dashboards went blank around 03:15 UTC and our on-call didn’t get the p95 alert. Can you confirm if data was lost?
2026-03-13 08:32 - Support (Asha): Acknowledged. Creating ticket and escalating to SRE/Platform. Please provide the route name and any IDs; we see anomalous retention sweeper activity.

2026-03-13 10:02 - SRE (Liam): Initial triage: retention-sweeper ran an emergency GC with experimental policy purge_high_volume=true at 02:58 UTC. Investigating whether per-tenant override was ignored.

2026-03-13 12:45 - Engineering (Tara): Confirmed a config mismatch pushed in canary yesterday (PR #4965) where default_retention_days was unintentionally lowered for dedicated tenants. Looking into rehydration options.
2026-03-14 09:08 - Support (Asha): Customer notified of ongoing recovery work and temporary workaround (alert health-checks added).
investigation_notes:
Timeline: 02:58 UTC retention-sweeper v1.7.0 executed GC that pruned events older than 7 days for several tenant buckets. FinSaaS had a per-customer override of 30d that appears not to have been applied due to a config layering bug introduced in PR #4965 (console-config merge step).

What we checked:
- retention-sweeper logs: confirmed purge_high_volume flag true and tenant override read path returned null for tenant_id finss-183.
- metrics-store (ClickHouse) ingestion logs: events were deleted by background cleanup job, not a downstream ingestion failure.
- Object store (S3): raw ingestion batches still exist for the period but were marked as eligible for GC and tombstoned by retention-sweeper metadata.
- Alerting evaluation: rule engine skipped evaluation when metric series absent; no fallback to raw ingestion stream.

Hypothesis: The config merge for dedicated tenants skipped the per-tenant retention file due to a path normalization regression on unix->container mount, causing default (7d) to apply. This triggered GC and caused both Console and alerting silence.

Next steps taken:
- Suspended retention-sweeper for affected tenant (finss-183) at 2026-03-13T11:20:00Z.
- Began rehydration from raw ingestion batches in S3 for last 48 hours; rehydrate job currently in progress (replay-restore job id rr-20260313-01).
- Rolling patch prepared to fix config merge logic (PR #4998) and add a hard guard to prevent sweeping tenants with per-tenant override present.
resolution_notes:
Workaround applied: retention-sweeper paused for finss-183 and an emergency rehydrate was executed to restore 48 hours of metrics and traces. Rehydrate completed at 2026-03-14T04:12:00Z. Console dashboards rebuilt; p95/p99 charts back-populated.

Fix rolled: PR #4998 merged and deployed to canary at 2026-03-14T02:30:00Z and promoted to prod at 2026-03-14T08:00:00Z. The patch ensures per-tenant retention files are validated and adds a kill-switch to require operator confirmation before sweeping >= 2x default volume.

Customer communication: FinSaaS notified of root cause and mitigation. Offered 30% credit for the impacted billing window and a follow-up architecture review for retention sizing.

Follow-ups:
- Add automated canary that validates per-tenant retention values against console UI before any retention job runs.
- Update runbook: retention GC emergency rollback steps (Confluence page).
